Simple Present Tense of the Verb Allow to Talk About Permitting Possibility
We can use the verb allow to talk about a thing, person, or event that permits something or someone to perform an activity.

We can use the verb allow when we are talking about permitting or giving the possibility to someone or something to execute or perform an action.

Form: subject + allow + direct object + infinitive form of the verb

Note that if the subject corresponds to the third person singular, you have to add -s to the verb.

Examples:
This command allows you to represent a Boolean value.

In the above mentioned case, there is something (the command) that permits the person (who is implicit) to represent a specific value in his programming code.

She allows her employees to work with C++ and C#.

In this new case, it's a person who permits other people to do something. This time, we can see that the sentence talks more about giving permission than helping or giving people the necessary tools to perform the mentioned action.
The index system allows you to look up for data you need.
Value type allows us to store data directly.

Alan: Carlo, I feel like there's something wrong with me; I still can't get my head around this C# stuff!
Carlo: What exactly is it that you don't get?
Alan: Well, I obviously understand that it's a versatile general-purpose computer programming language that closely follows the C and C++ languages, but when it comes to the data types I'm totally lost!
Carlo: Well, the important ones are really quite simple. Let's start with value types; they will allow us to store data directly, such as numbers, alphabets, and floating point numbers, and they can be directly assigned a value.

Alan: Ok, I can see how they would be useful.
Carlo: Then you have the reference type. The reference type does not store data directly but contains references to all of the variables. In other words, it refers to the memory location.
Alan: So it's like an indexed file system that allows you to look up for the data you need.
Carlo: Yes, something like that. Then there's the pointer type. Pointer type is very easy for anyone who can use C or C++ because they have the same capabilities; they store the address of another type.

Alan: All of those seem easy enough. What about object, dynamic, and string types?
Carlo: Object type is probably the most important of those three. It is the ultimate base class for all types in C# common systems. It can be assigned the values of any other data types. However, before assigning values, it needs converting. This conversion is called “boxing,” or “unboxing” in the other direction.
Alan: That's a seriously useful data type!
Carlo: It certainly is. The dynamic type is also useful as you can store any data type inside it. Finally string type; this type allows you to assign any string values to a variable, making larger chunks of data more accessible.
Alan: Thank you very much, Carlo. I'm going to practice some coding to consolidate the information you gave me!
